name: Dorabella cipher, Edward Elgar to Dora Penny, 14 July 1897
ciphertext: ABCDE FGDHA IJKLJ MJJFB BJNGO GNIP
GJGFQ DHRSC JJCFN KGJIJ FTPKL QHHQI P
CPFUP CLUUN PCJFU KPNDB NPFDL ED
ciphertext_source: Schmeh's letter transcription, Cipherbrain post 26 (2017, sources/schmeh/posts/26-dorabella.txt): 24 symbols (1-3 semicircles in 8 orientations) mapped to A-X in order of first appearance; a dot after the fifth symbol of line 3. Image: Elgar Birthplace Museum; the orientation of some symbols is disputed (Wikipedia, 24 Sept 2026).
alphabet: 24 symbols = 3 arc-counts x 8 orientations; 87 symbols; lines 29 / 31 / 27

constraints.known_key_fragment: Elgar used the same symbol alphabet in a 1920s notebook to write MARCO ELGAR and a Liszt reference (Bauer, Unsolved!); that mapping applied to the 1897 note does not yield English
constraints.negative_on_file: Wase, Cryptologia 49:1 (2025): solvers that read 87-letter English/Latin monoalphabetic ciphers at up to 98.7% fail on Dorabella, so not a MASC of English or Latin

cheap_tests_in_order: 1. Index rule (Urquhart lesson a): read each symbol as a number under the four natural encodings (orientation 1-8; arcs 1-3; 3(o-1)+a in 1-24; 8(a-1)+o in 1-24) and index into the words of the letter the note was enclosed with (Alice Elgar to Mrs Penny, July 1897, printed in Dora Powell, Edward Elgar: Memories of a Variation, 1937) and into the Enigma Variations' dedication texts; take first letters; judge in English. Control: the same rule on 200 random 87-symbol strings. Cost $2, Sonnet, once the letter text is on disk (Powell 1937 is in copyright; IA lending, an ASKS row).

2. Apply the notebook key values to the 87 symbols, then test the result as phonetic English (Dora Penny's memoir says Elgar used a private argot) with a phoneme-level scorer rather than the letter 4-gram; control: the notebook key on random symbol strings. Cost $2, Sonnet.

3. Musical reading: 8 orientations x 3 arcs as 24 pitches (3 octaves of a scale) and compare the resulting melody with the incipit of Variation X 'Dorabella' (1899) and with Elgar's 1897 works; control: random symbol strings against the same incipits. Cost $2, Sonnet.
None of these has a published negative; all three are cheap and self-judging.
matched_control: random 87-symbol strings over 24 symbols under the same rule
value: very high in fame; low prior after 129 years and Wase 2025
status_24_Sept_2026: open; claimed solutions (Sams 1970, Roberts, Henderson 2011, Packwood 2020, Belanger 2025-26) none accepted; Bourdeau: famous list, not attempted
schema_note: cheap_tests_in_order are proposals (rule 10: an approach is not a claim); a test actually run is under cheap_test_done with its control
